dedupe_keys.name: ngsim vehicle trajectories and supporting data

description: The Next Generation Simulation program of the Federal Highway Administration developed open behavioural algorithms for microscopic traffic simulation and collected data sets to develop and validate them. Its researchers recorded detailed vehicle trajectories on southbound US 101 and Lankershim Boulevard in Los Angeles, eastbound I-80 in Emeryville, California, and Peachtree Street in Atlanta, using networks of synchronised digital video cameras; the NGVIDEO software transcribed each vehicle's position every tenth of a second, giving lane positions and locations relative to other vehicles. Supporting metadata and site video data sets are attached. Coverage is four study sites in the United States. Access: free from the U.S. DOT ITS Public Data Hub as tabular export under CC BY-SA 3.0; the trajectory table was last updated in August 2018. Caveats: each site covers short periods only, at four locations. The data support calibration and validation of car-following and lane-changing models in microscopic simulators. They complement the FHWA TGSIM trajectories catalogued here and SUMO.
